chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal narrated to us, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Thabit ibn Abu Safiyyah, from Sa'd al-Khaffaf, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

to a man: If you do not obey your Creator, then do not eat of His Sustenance. And if you are a supporter of His Enemy, then leave His Realm. And if you are not content with His Decree and Divine Decree, then seek a Lord other than Him.
ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions Imam Ali gives for properly acknowledging God's lordship through obedience, allegiance, and contentment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Tawhid, Imam Ali (AS) establishes a logical triad connecting worship, allegiance, and contentment to the validity of one's relationship with Allah. He argues that disobedience invalidates the consumption of divine sustenance, allegiance to God's enemies necessitates leaving His dominion, and dissatisfaction with divine decree implies seeking an alternative lord. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the coherence between belief, action, and inner acceptance of Qadr.
